_comment: Unit types. Every regiment is a unit of 1000 people taken from the population (see levies in data/laws.json) and armed as one of these. category: foot (infantry, ranged, swordsmen, pikemen...), mounted (chariots, cavalry, knights... and tanks once there are motor vehicles) or siege (rams, catapults, trebuchets, cannon, artillery: powerful but very vulnerable, and manned by soldiers; each needs a regiment of foot to screen it, or it adds nothing to a battle and is lost if the battle is). attack: strength in battle (a regiment of spearmen is 1). defense: how well it keeps its men alive (losses are divided by it). siege: power against fortifications. speed: km a day on the march (an army marches at its slowest regiment's pace). cost: gold to equip a regiment when it is raised. upkeep: gold a month while it is under arms. requires: a condition (as for flags in data/countries/EGY.json), for now the date the kind of unit appears in the world; requires_text says it in words. share: its share of a new country's levies, in percent.

units.name: Spearmen
units.description: Villagers with spear and hide shield: the mass of every Bronze Age army.

units.name: Archers
units.description: Bowmen who shower the enemy from behind the spears.

units.name: Slingers
units.description: Shepherds with slings: cheap, light and quick to raise.

units.name: Swordsmen
units.description: Warriors with the long bronze swords the Sea Peoples brought: deadly at close quarters.

units.name: Hoplites
units.description: Heavy spearmen shoulder to shoulder behind round shields.

units.name: Pikemen
units.description: A phalanx of long pikes no horseman can break.

units.name: Legionaries
units.description: Drilled swordsmen with javelins and great shields.

units.name: Crossbowmen
units.description: Bolts that pierce mail, shot by men with little training.

units.name: Musketeers
units.description: Gunpowder in the hands of foot soldiers.

units.name: Riflemen
units.description: Rifled guns that kill at hundreds of paces.

units.name: Infantry
units.description: Machine guns, trenches and lorries: the foot soldier of the motor age.

units.name: Chariots
units.description: Light two-horse chariots with an archer and a driver: the pride of the Bronze Age kings.

units.name: Heavy chariots
units.description: Four-horse chariots with a crew of three, built to smash infantry.

units.name: Horsemen
units.description: Men who fight from the horse's back.

units.name: Horse archers
units.description: Riders of the steppe who shoot at the gallop.

units.name: Cataphracts
units.description: Horse and rider clad in armour from head to hoof.

units.name: Knights
units.description: Armoured lancers on great horses, with stirrups to take the shock.

units.name: Cuirassiers
units.description: Armoured horsemen with sword and pistol.

units.name: Tanks
units.description: Motor vehicles armoured and armed: the horse's heir.
units.requires_text: Needs motor vehicles, from about 1916 AD

units.name: Rams and ladders
units.description: Battering rams, ladders and sappers' tools, carried by the men who work them.

units.name: Siege towers
units.description: Wheeled towers and armoured rams, rolled up to the walls.

units.name: Catapults
units.description: Torsion engines that hurl stones and bolts.

units.name: Trebuchets
units.description: Great counterweight engines that bring down walls.

units.name: Cannon
units.description: Bronze and iron guns: no wall stands against them for long.

units.name: Artillery
units.description: Rifled guns firing shells from miles away.
